A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S-VCO/MVC research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM finetuning evaluations, ablations, qualitative examples and a perplexity analysis of 1,000 image pairs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised benchmark scores and visual-dependency results.

M1.justification: The attending and rejecting losses, symmetrical objective in Equations 3-7, visual filtering and two-step language augmentation remain unchanged. Appendix C's prompt refinements do not establish a different algorithm or regenerated dataset.

E1.justification: Training retains MVC, sourced from CounterCurate and FineCops-Ref, and VLFeedback. The same eight evaluation benchmarks and no-image comparisons remain. NaturalBench is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DPO and mDPO trained on VLF and MVC for both backbones. The raw-data, asymmetric VCO and SFT comparisons also retain their membership.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1 and Appendices A-B retain the splits, model sizes, training budgets, preprocessing thresholds, checkpoint-selection procedure, evaluation judges and decoding temperature. Neither PDF documents a protocol change explaining the revised MMVP scores.

E4.justification: The existing analysis of performance gains versus visual dependency is revised: Figure 6 moves MMVP from dependency 27.54 to 100 and updates the fitted trends. The filtering, symmetry and SFT ablations and Figure 5 case studies retain their questions and comparisons.

E5.justification: The existing perplexity distributions and shaded regression-variability bands remain. There is no added seed information, repeated-run count, significance testing or new uncertainty-reporting procedure; changed band values accompany revised results.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises every MMVP score: BASE/S-VCO change from 56.0/56.0 to 21.3/25.3 for LV-1.5, and from 69.0/73.0 to 41.3/50.7 for LV-INT. LV-INT's BASE TextVQA changes from 58.62 to 59.45. S-VCO's aggregate improvements change from 12.17% to 14.26% and 8.59% to 10.47%, respectively. Figure 6 changes MMVP dependency from 27.54 to 100. These materially revise the reported evidence; they do not establish gains from a changed method under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7 and the definition of visual dependency retain the same mathematical content. No assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: symmetrical visual contrastive optimization, the MVC dataset, reduced hallucinations and stronger visually dependent performance while preserving general capabilities.

C2.justification: The explanations of visual neglect, shortcut learning, symmetry, SFT degradation and ScienceQA's weak visual dependence remain. The revised MMVP discussion applies the existing visual-dependency interpretation; no new mechanism, applicability boundary or substantive limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 removes the footnotes specifying exact HuggingFace checkpoint identifiers. Appendix C revises the displayed second-step augmentation prompt, including repetition of the input fields after the examples. Hardware, hyperparameters and dataset-access information otherwise remain.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds NaturalBench (Li et al., 2024a) and Peng et al.'s fine-grained vision-language study, connecting confounding image-pair failures to Figure 2. The InstructBLIP citation and reference are removed. The principal positioning against DPO-based approaches remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the preliminaries, results discussion and related work, plus prompt wording and capitalization edits. The section order, overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 6 update their plotted profiles and trends. Figure 6 changes benchmark positions, axis range and label presentation, while Appendix C resizes the second prompt box and its text. The figure/table inventory and overall layout remain stable.

improvement.justification: v2 improves numerical consistency: v1's printed LV-INT/S-VCO scores imply approximately 8.75% average improvement, although Table 1 reports 8.59%; v2's revised scores reproduce its reported 10.47%. Updated plots and added related-work context also improve the account. The gain is limited because the substantial MMVP revisions remain unexplained and exact checkpoint identifiers are removed.
